newsitem.title: UK: Copper and aluminium slide in late LME, end down.
newsitem.headline: Copper and aluminium slide in late LME, end down.

text.p: Late liquidation in copper on Monday restrained the LME market which had faltered earlier just under $2,050, and by the close of business prices were softer.
Traders said a similar reaction was seen in aluminium, which also fell away during the latter part of the trading session, although the rest of the metal complex ended on a positive note.
Generally, copper is pausing on technical considerations, having briefly recorded a fresh seven-week high of $2,042 on Monday, with the main upside target seen around $2,070.
Warehouse stock falls, which are driving the market to some extent, are expected to continue on Tuesday, traders added.
Traders said metal will again be drawn down from LME European warehouses, with some destined for the U.S. Hamburg is likely to show a sizeble decline.

Meanwhile, the fighting between Tutsi rebels and government troops in Zaire is not having an impact yet, as the country's key copper and cobalt areas are well south of the eastern Zairean city of Bukavu.
Last three months business was at $2,016 a tonne, down $12 from Friday. The cash/threes backwardation eased in slightly to $26/31.
Aluminium mirrored copper and reversed direction, with chartists saying the market may need to retrace towards $1,400 to consolidate before significantly moving upwards.
LME stocks are seen lower on Tuesday, although this may not influence prices. Last business was at $1,415.50, down $19.

Nickel was bolstered by short-covering after an upside chart break through the 100-day moving average which triggered fresh investment fund buying. Despite a brief setback in the mid-afternoon the market still ended the session on a high note.
Last kerb trade was at $7,409 a tonne, up $139 from Friday, with $7,600 seen as the next upside technical objective.
Zinc prices pushed through the $1,050 level, capitalising on some investment fund buying and constructive charts, and last trade was at $1,054, a $15 gain from pre-weekend levels.
Lead trading was quiet, although intermittent fund interest kept prices in the plus column as the market built on last week's advances. Final trade was at $746, up $8.
Tin held in a narrow $6,000/6,020 range, concluding the day at the lower end of this band, still up $10 from Friday.
Alloy was quoted at $1,265/70 a tonne, against last week's close of $1,282.
